headline: NASA selects Relativity Space for 2028 Mars mission, challenging SpaceX
summary: Eric Schmidt's Relativity Space will build a spacecraft for the Aeolus mission, aiming to provide the first daily global view of Mars' atmosphere, potentially beating SpaceX to the Red Planet.
details: NASA has awarded a contract to Relativity Space, the rocket maker backed by former Google executive chair Eric Schmidt, to build and launch a spacecraft to Mars by 2028. This mission could see Relativity Space reach the Red Planet before SpaceX.

The mission, dubbed Aeolus, will house four scientific instruments to measure and image Mars from orbit. It aims to provide the first daily, global view of dust, winds, and temperature in the Martian atmosphere, enhancing safety for future landers and human missions.

This contract follows NASA's model of public-private partnerships, similar to deals with SpaceX for ISS cargo or Firefly Aerospace for Moon landers. NASA handles the scientific objectives, while the private company provides the infrastructure, allowing the agency to stretch its budget.

The 2028 launch timeline is ambitious, requiring Relativity to design and build the spacecraft and complete its Terran R rocket on a tight schedule. While NASA did not disclose the payment, such partnerships involve companies taking on some development costs for broader commercial opportunities.

Relativity Space, founded in 2015, focuses on 3D printing for cheaper rocket construction. Its first design, Terran-1, failed mid-flight in March 2023, leading the company to pivot to the larger Terran R design.

Eric Schmidt acquired a majority stake in Relativity Space last year after the company faced fundraising challenges, installing himself as CEO. He has expressed interest in orbital data centers and is reportedly using Relativity to launch his family philanthropy's space telescope, Lazuili.

This mission sets up a potential rivalry with Elon Musk's SpaceX, which has long-stated Martian ambitions but has not yet sent its own mission to Mars. If Aeolus launches on schedule, it could become the first private mission to reach the Red Planet.

headline: DeepSeek Introduces Vision
summary: DeepSeek has unveiled its new Vision model, expanding its AI capabilities to include advanced image understanding and analysis. This development marks a significant step in multimodal AI research.
details: DeepSeek, known for its open-source language models, has officially launched DeepSeek Vision. This new model integrates advanced visual perception, allowing it to process and interpret image data alongside text.

The introduction of Vision aims to bridge the gap between textual and visual AI, enabling more comprehensive understanding of complex information. It is expected to enhance applications requiring both language and image comprehension.

While specific technical details are yet to be fully disclosed, the model is anticipated to offer robust performance in tasks such as object recognition, scene understanding, and visual question answering. This could unlock new possibilities for developers and researchers.

This move positions DeepSeek more firmly in the competitive landscape of multimodal AI development, challenging existing models from other major tech players. The community awaits further benchmarks and practical applications.
